notes: Cross-language contract for the desktop VM core (apps/builder-mac FlagshipBuilderCore/VM <-> apps/builder-windows src/VM <-> apps/builder-linux vm). Both test suites MUST consume this file so the cores cannot drift — the same role engine/golden/preseed-vectors.json plays for the preseed engine. States: created | installing | installed | awaitingPhoneUnlock | running | stopped | failed:install | failed:run. Events: startInstall | installSucceeded | installFailed | powerOn | guestUnlocked | powerOff | runtimeFailed. Effects: attachInstallerISO | detachInstallerISO | startVirtualMachine | stopVirtualMachine. 'sealed' mirrors VMConfig.awaitsPhoneUnlockAtBoot; transitions listing no 'sealed' key must hold for BOTH values.

installVerdict.notes: A hypervisor-level clean guest-stop during install is ambiguous (success poweroff / completed-install reboot / never-booted all look identical), so the verdict is duration-gated: elapsed >= minPlausibleInstallSeconds => installSucceeded, else installFailed with an actionable reason. Edge: exactly the minimum counts as success. Verdict tokens pin the EVENT chosen, not the failure prose (messages are per-platform).

resourcePlan.notes: gib = 2^30. Constants: default 6 GiB (4 GiB on hosts with at most 16 GiB RAM), floor 4 GiB, host reserve 4 GiB, absolute max 8 VMs, default main disk 64 GiB.

diskDurability.notes: How every hosted server's writable main disk is attached. Two VMs were left with zeroed system files by guest writes the host never flushed. Virtualization.framework (Mac): host-cached, every guest flush reaches the disk. QEMU (Windows, Linux): writeback cache with guest flushes honoured (never cache=unsafe or cache.no-flush), thread-pool I/O (works on every filesystem and on Windows, unlike O_DIRECT), and guest TRIM freeing space in the host image. Each QEMU port asserts every key=value below on the main -drive.

serverHealth.notes: A hosted server's own health report, read from .com by the order serial that created it (GET /api/order/<serial>/health, control-plane serverHealth.ts). 'response' is the raw body; each port reads it for serverDomain and renders the verdict at nowMs. null = nothing to show (another server, no report yet, malformed). Copy matches the phone apps (BoxHealth.verdict on iOS).

applianceSeed.notes: The one-use specialization seed a new hosted server reads (packages/flagship-builder appliance.ts encodeApplianceSeed is the reference; the guest specializer checks the header's length and body SHA-256 before decoding). The seed is sizeBytes long: the 80-byte ASCII header, the compact JSON body (keys in this order, no escaped '/'), then zeros. Node and Windows reproduce 'body' byte for byte; the Mac's JSONEncoder writes an equivalent body the guest accepts the same way.

nameValidation.notes: Bundle names are server FQDNs. Allowed: lowercase a-z, 0-9, '.', '-'; non-empty; not '.' or '..'; no LEADING dot; no TRAILING dot (the trailing-dot rejection is one deliberate tightening over the original Mac validate() — Win32 silently strips trailing dots and no real FQDN ends in one; the Mac side should adopt it).

bootEvidence.notes: Studio decides a sealed guest has unlocked ONLY from the box's own signed health report on .com, never by fetching https://<server domain>/ from the host: the name does not exist until the box registers it, and a lookup before then is cached as NXDOMAIN by home routers for the zone's negative TTL (30 min seen on Windows 2026-10-18), leaving Studio on 'Waiting for you to unlock' on a healthy box. provesBoxIsUp = the daemon is active, the relay tunnel is up, the report was received after this boot began (receivedAtMs >= poweredOnAtMs), the guest's uptime fits inside the time since this boot began (+60 s slack, so a previous boot's report is never taken), and it is under 5 minutes old at nowMs. A server without an order serial has no health report and falls back to probing its name.

awaitingUnlockCopy.notes: The sidebar/detail copy while a guest is sealed, identical on all three Studios. The phone, not Studio, decides whether a restart needs an approval: the key the phone leaves at its first approval can be missing (on Windows 2026-10-18 a restart still asked the phone while Studio said 'Nothing to approve'), so no line promises that nobody has to act.
awaitingUnlockCopy.stalled: Taking longer than expected — the box may not have reached the network, or it may be waiting for you to approve the unlock on your phone. Check that it's online, or power off and retry.
awaitingUnlockCopy.unlocksOnItsOwn: Unlocking its disk with the key your phone left it. If your phone asks you to approve, approve it there.
awaitingUnlockCopy.firstBoot: The disk is sealed — approve the first unlock on your phone. After that it should unlock on its own; if your phone asks again, approve it there.
awaitingUnlockCopy.approveEveryBoot: The disk is sealed — approve the unlock on your phone.
